source_refs.note: Book p. 289-290: 11.3.1 criteria for scalar and vector-valued functions, printed Examples 2 and 3 (shown as Examples 4 and 5)

blocks.text: Is page par kitab woh nishaniyan (criteria) deti hai jin se hum kisi bhi function ko dekh kar bata sakte hain ke woh scalar hai ya vector-valued. Har qism ki teen nishaniyan hain, aur har qism ke baad ek misaal. Aaiye pehle scalar function ki nishaniyan dekhte hain.

(i) Scalar-valued function ek hi numerical value deta hai (jaise ek real number).
(ii) Scalar-valued functions aam tor par chhote (lowercase) harf se likhe jate hain (jaise \(f(x)\)).
(iii) Scalar-valued functions temperature ya potential energy jaisi miqdaron ko bayan karte hain.

blocks.title: Numbering note (ours)
blocks.text: Is page ki do misaalen kitab mein "Example 2" aur "Example 3" ke naam se chhapi hain (kitab ne 11.2.1 mein ginti dobara shuru ki thi). Is portal par yeh Example 4 aur Example 5 hain.

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: In a heat transfer problem, the temperature \(T(x, y, z) = 100 - x^{2} - y^{2} - z^{2}\) describes the temperature at a point \((x, y, z)\) in a three-dimensional space.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(T(x, y, z) = 100 - x^{2} - y^{2} - z^{2}\), point \((x, y, z)\) par temperature.
Maloom karna: \(T\) scalar-valued hai ya vector-valued (kitab ki "Identification").
Tareeqa: upar wale criteria (i)-(iii) lagayenge: output kya hai, likha kaise gaya hai, aur kis cheez ko bayan karta hai. Sab se pehle input aur output ko alag alag pehchaante hain, kyun ke yahin students aksar uljhte hain.

Step 1: Input
Input ek position \((x, y, z)\) hai, yani teen numbers.
Kyun: input se qism tay nahin hoti, lekin hum ise alag likh lete hain taa ke ise ghalti se output na samajh lein. Teen inputs dekh kar "vector" kehne ka dil chahta hai, magar ruk jaiye!

Step 2: Output (criterion (i))
\(100 - x^{2} - y^{2} - z^{2}\) ek real number hai. Misaal ke tor par (hamari values):
\[T(1, 2, 3) = 100 - 1 - 4 - 9 = 86\]
Kyun: real numbers ko square, jama aur tafreeq karne se hamesha ek hi real number milta hai, jis ki koi direction nahin.

Step 3: Identification
Function ek position \((x, y, z)\) leta hai aur ek hi number \(T\) (degrees mein temperature) deta hai, is liye yeh scalar-valued hai.
Kyun: criterion (i) poora hua; saath (ii) \(T\) saade (bold nahin) harf se likha hai, aur (iii) temperature scalar miqdar hai.

Step 4: Kahan kaam aata hai
Engineers aise functions se materials mein garmi ki taqseem (heat distribution) ka model banate hain, maslan electronic devices ke cooling systems design karte waqt.
Kyun: \(T\) origin par sab se zyada, \(T = 100\), hai aur jaise jaise \(x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}\) barhta hai, kam hota jata hai. Yani garam markaz (center) se garmi bahar ki taraf phailti aur kam hoti hai, jaise mobile ka processor beech mein garam aur kinaron par thanda.

Tasdeeq:
Teenon criteria ek hi jawab dete hain: bahar ek number, saada harf, temperature. Output mein na \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) hain na angle brackets, is liye \(T\) vector-valued ho hi nahin sakta.
blocks.answer: \(T(x, y, z)\) scalar-valued function hai: yeh position \((x, y, z)\) leta hai aur sirf ek number, yani temperature, deta hai.

blocks.text:
(i) Vector-valued function ek vector deta hai, jo aksar ordered tuple (tarteeb wali list) ya component functions ki shakal mein likha jata hai (jaise 2D mein \(\mathbf{f}(t) = \langle f_{1}(t), f_{2}(t)\rangle\) ya 3D mein \(\mathbf{g}(t) = \langle g_{1}(t), g_{2}(t), g_{3}(t)\rangle\)).
(ii) Vector-valued functions aksar bold harf ya arrow ke saath likhe jate hain (jaise \(\mathbf{f}(t)\) ya \(\vec{f}(t)\)).
(iii) Vector-valued functions position, velocity aur force jaisi miqdaron ko bayan karte hain.

blocks.title: Example 5
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \langle\cos(t), \sin(t), t\rangle\).
Maloom karna: is ki qism, vector \(\mathbf{r}(\pi/2)\), aur yeh kaun si shakal banata hai.
Tareeqa: vector-valued functions ke criteria (i)-(iii) lagayenge, phir har component mein \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) rakhenge.

Step 1: Input aur output
Input ek scalar variable \(t\) hai (aksar time), aur output 3-dimensional vector hai.
Kyun: criterion (i): output teen component functions \(\cos t\), \(\sin t\), \(t\) ki tarteeb wali list hai; criterion (ii): naam \(\mathbf{r}\) bold mein likha hai.

Step 2: \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) par value
\[\mathbf{r}\Big(\frac{\pi}{2}\Big) = \Big\langle\cos\frac{\pi}{2}, \sin\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\Big\rangle\]
\[= \Big\langle 0, 1, \frac{\pi}{2}\Big\rangle\]
Kyun: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\) aur \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\); teesra component khud \(t\) hai, is liye wahan \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) hi aata hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos\) aur \(\sin\) ki values ulat dena yahan sab se aam ghalti hai. Unit circle yaad kijiye: \(90^{\circ}\) par point \((0, 1)\) hai.

Step 3: Output ka matlab
Output ek vector hai jo 3D space mein point \(\big(0, 1, \frac{\pi}{2}\big)\) ki taraf ishara karta hai.
Kyun: origin se draw kiya gaya position vector usi point par khatam hota hai jis ke coordinates vector ke components hain.

Step 4: Kaun si shakal banti hai
Yeh function helix banata hai.
Kyun: \(x^{2} + y^{2} = \cos^{2}t + \sin^{2}t = 1\), yani upar se dekhein to point radius 1 wale circle par ghoomta hai, aur \(z = t\) mustaqil barhta hai. Yeh bilkul Example 2 wale drone ka raasta hai, bas radius 1 aur har radian par 1 unit chadhai.

Tasdeeq:
\(\mathbf{r}(0) = \langle 1, 0, 0\rangle\) aur \(\mathbf{r}(\pi) = \langle -1, 0, \pi\rangle\): point aadha chakkar ghooma aur \(\pi\) upar utha, jaisa helix mein hona chahiye.
blocks.answer: \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) vector-valued hai (ek scalar input, 3-dimensional vector output); \(\mathbf{r}(\pi/2) = \langle 0, 1, \frac{\pi}{2}\rangle\), jo 3D space mein ek point hai; curve helix hai.

blocks.text: Ab dono qismon ki nishaniyan saath saath rakh kar dekhiye; exam se pehle yeh table ek nazar mein dohrayi (revise) ki ja sakti hai:

rows: Output: ek vector (components ki tarteeb wali list)
blocks.caption: Hamara khulasa: dono ki pehchaan saath saath

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Kisi bhi function ke liye teen sawal: (1) Bahar kya aata hai, ek number ya kai components? (2) Kaise likha hai, saada harf ya bold/arrow, \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) ya \(\langle\ \rangle\)? (3) Kya bayan karta hai, sirf size ya size ke saath direction? Faisla sawal (1) karta hai; (2) aur (3) aam tor par usi ki tasdeeq karte hain.
Yaad rahe: likhne ka andaz ek aadat hai, qanoon nahin. Koi vector function saade harf se bhi likh sakta hai, is liye hamesha output se tasdeeq karein.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Khud sochiye: \(V(x, y) = \langle x, -y\rangle\) kis qism ka hai? Input do numbers, output do components wala vector, to vector-valued (yeh har point par ek arrow deta hai, jaise hawa ka rukh). Aur \(E(t) = \frac{1}{2}t^{2}\)? Ek number, to scalar.
Yaad rakhiye: notation (likhne ka andaz) madadgar hai, magar aakhri faisla hamesha output karta hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Hamari taraf se misaal (kitab ka sawal nahin): neeche teen functions ki qism bataiye.
(a) \(\mathbf{u}(t) = \langle e^{t}, 2\rangle\): output do components wala vector, to vector-valued.
(b) \(m(t) = |\langle t, 1\rangle| = \sqrt{t^{2} + 1}\): yeh vector ki lambai hai, jo ek number hai, to scalar. Ghor kijiye: andar vector hai, magar bahar sirf number aa raha hai.
(c) \(\vec{F}(t) = t\hat{i} - t\hat{k}\): arrow wala naam aur \(\hat{i}, \hat{k}\), output vector, to vector-valued.

Ab socho ke yeh pehchaan aage kahan kaam aayegi. Exercise 11.1 ke Question 8 mein bilkul yahi sawal hain: function diya hoga aur aap ko wajah ke saath batana hoga ke woh scalar hai ya vector-valued. Jawab likhne ka achha tareeqa: "Output ek real number hai, is liye scalar function" ya "Output components wala vector hai, is liye vector-valued". Sirf naam likh dena kaafi nahin; wajah (reasoning) bhi likhiye, kyun ke sawal yahi maangta hai.

Aur ek dilchasp baat: scalar aur vector functions aapas mein jure bhi hote hain. Vector function ki lambai (magnitude) scalar function hai, aur kai scalar functions ko jor kar vector function banta hai. Isi liye pehchaan zaroori hai: pehle qism pehchaano, phir sahi tareeqa lagao.

Kitab ki dono misaalon ko phir se yaad kijiye, kyun ke yeh dono qismon ke "model" hain. Temperature wali misaal mein input teen numbers the magar output ek number; is liye scalar. Helix wali misaal mein input ek number tha magar output teen numbers ka vector; is liye vector-valued. Dekhiye, dono misaalen jaan boojh kar ulti chuni gayi hain: pehli mein zyada inputs, doosri mein zyada outputs. Kitab yahi sikhana chahti hai ke inputs ki ginti se dhoka na khayein.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Khud sochiye: \(T(0, 0, 0)\) kya hai, aur \(T(10, 0, 0)\)? \(T(0, 0, 0) = 100\) (sab se garam jagah), aur \(T(10, 0, 0) = 100 - 100 = 0\). Yani markaz se 10 unit door temperature zero ho jata hai. Jitne points markaz se barabar faasle par hain (ek sphere par), un sab ka temperature same hai. Phir bhi har point ka jawab sirf ek number hai: scalar.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Scalar function: ek numerical value; saada chhota harf; temperature, potential energy.
2. Vector-valued function: vector \(\langle f_{1}(t), f_{2}(t)\rangle\) ya \(\langle g_{1}(t), g_{2}(t), g_{3}(t)\rangle\); bold ya arrow; position, velocity, force.
3. \(T(x, y, z) = 100 - x^{2} - y^{2} - z^{2}\) ke teen inputs magar ek output, is liye scalar-valued.
4. \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \langle\cos t, \sin t, t\rangle\) ka ek input aur 3D vector output, is liye vector-valued; yeh helix banata hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(T(x, y, z)\) ko vector-valued kehna kyun ke us ka input 3D point hai: sirf output dekhna hai.
2. \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\) aur \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\) ulat kar \(\mathbf{r}(\pi/2) = \langle 1, 0, \frac{\pi}{2}\rangle\) likh dena.
3. Teesre component mein \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) likhna bhool jana: teesra component khud \(t\) hai.
